Sewer Line Repair in Sarasota, FL

Slow drains, sewage smell or a soggy spot in the yard can mean a broken sewer lateral. SRQ Leak Pros connects you with a local pro for camera inspection and sewer line repair.

Call (941) 393-1012
  • Sarasota & Manatee counties
  • Service lines, slabs, sewers & pools
  • Homes, condos & businesses
  • Independent local providers

Quick answer: Sewer line repair in Sarasota fixes the private lateral that carries wastewater from your home to the public sewer. A pro runs a sewer camera inspection to find cracks, roots or sags, then repairs one spot, lines the pipe from inside, bursts in a new pipe, or digs and replaces it.

Your sewer lateral is the other service line on your property. It carries everything that goes down your drains to the public sewer main or to a septic tank. Many older Sarasota homes still have cast iron or clay laterals, and some mid-century homes had Orangeburg pipe. When a lateral cracks, it can leak into the soil, let roots in, or back sewage into the house.

Signs of a broken sewer line

SignLikely cause
Several drains slow or backing up at onceBlockage or break in the main lateral
Gurgling toilets when a sink drainsVenting problem or partial blockage
Sewage smell in the yard or houseCrack or broken joint
One very green, lush patch of lawnWastewater feeding the grass
Soggy soil or a sinkhole along the lineCollapsed or separated pipe
Recurring clogs after cleaningRoots or a sag in the line

What sewer line repair includes

  • A sewer camera inspection with video you can see
  • Line locating to mark the lateral's path and depth
  • Finding the cleanout or adding one for access
  • Cleaning or root cutting if the line is blocked
  • A written repair plan with the defect locations
  • An 811 ticket before any digging
  • The repair, lining or replacement
  • A final camera pass to confirm the fix
  • Backfill and surface restoration, if quoted

Sewer pipe materials in Sarasota homes

  • Cast iron. Heavy metal pipe common under older slabs and in yards. It scales, cracks and rusts through over time.
  • Clay (vitrified clay). Used in older laterals. Joints let roots in.
  • Orangeburg. A tar-soaked wood fiber pipe from the mid-1900s that can soften and flatten.
  • PVC. Modern plastic pipe used in most newer homes and repairs.

How sewer line repair works, step by step

  1. Camera inspection. A camera on a cable runs through the cleanout to find each defect and measure its distance.
  2. Locate. A transmitter on the camera head lets the pro mark the spot on the ground.
  3. Clear the line. Roots and buildup are cut or jetted so the pipe can be judged clearly.
  4. Choose the method. Spot repair, lining, bursting or open-cut replacement.
  5. Permit and 811. Required permits are pulled and buried utilities are marked.
  6. Repair. The chosen fix is made.
  7. Re-inspect. A final camera run confirms the line is open and sound.

Repair methods compared

MethodHow it worksGood fit when
Spot repairDig at one defect and replace that sectionOne break in an otherwise sound pipe
Cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) liningA resin-soaked liner is cured inside the old pipeCracks and joint leaks, but the pipe still holds shape
Pipe burstingA new pipe is pulled through, splitting the old oneThe old pipe is badly damaged but the path is clear
Open-cut replacementDig the full length and lay new PVCSags, collapses or very shallow lines

Wikipedia describes CIPP as a trenchless rehabilitation method that creates a jointless, seamless pipe inside the existing one. It is used in sewer, water and gas lines. For more on trenchless methods, read the trenchless replacement guide.

Roots, sags and Florida soil

Sandy soil settles, which can create a sag, or "belly," where waste collects. Palm and ficus roots seek out moisture at cracked joints. Hurricanes and heavy rain can shift soil around old pipe. A camera inspection shows which of these is the real problem, so you don't pay for the wrong fix.

Who owns which part of the sewer?

Ownership usually splits at the public sewer main or at a property-line cleanout. The utility maintains its main. The owner maintains the lateral on private property. The City of Sarasota's utilities page explains how it handles sewer blockages and asks residents to report problems at manholes. Check your utility's rules before work starts.

Homes on a septic tank have no public lateral, but the line from the house to the tank still needs the same care. Septic systems are their own specialty.

Is it your lateral or the city main?

A backup can start in your pipe or in the public main. A few clues help you tell. If only your home backs up and the neighbors are fine, the problem is usually in your lateral. If several homes on the street back up at once, or a manhole is overflowing, report it to your utility. A camera inspection from your cleanout shows exactly where the blockage or break sits, and how far it is from the house.

Cleanouts and why they matter

A cleanout is a capped pipe, usually near the house or the property line, that gives direct access to the sewer lateral. It lets a pro run a camera or clear a clog without pulling a toilet. Many older homes don't have one, or it's buried under landscaping. Adding a cleanout during a repair makes future inspections faster and cheaper.

How to prevent sewer line problems

  • Don't flush wipes, even ones labeled "flushable"
  • Keep grease, oil and food scraps out of drains
  • Plant trees and large shrubs away from the lateral's path
  • Have older cast iron or clay lines camera-inspected before buying a home
  • Ask about a backwater valve if your home is low compared to the street
  • Clear slow drains early instead of waiting for a backup

Buying a home with an old sewer line

A standard home inspection usually doesn't look inside the sewer lateral. If the home you're buying was built with cast iron, clay or Orangeburg pipe, ask for a sewer camera inspection before closing. The video shows roots, cracks, sags and breaks, and how far each one is from the cleanout. You can use the findings to plan a repair, ask for a price change or budget for lining. Keep the video for your records.

Sewer backups and cleanup

Sewage carries bacteria, so a backup inside the home needs careful cleanup. Keep children and pets away from the area, and avoid touching wastewater without gloves. A sewer line pro fixes the pipe, while a water damage or sanitation company handles cleanup of floors and walls. Check whether your policy has a sewer backup endorsement before you need it.

What affects the cost

No price is listed, because sewer jobs vary widely. Ask for a written estimate. These factors matter most:

  • Length and depth of the lateral
  • Pipe material and the number of defects
  • Method: spot repair, lining, bursting or open cut
  • Access: under a driveway, slab or landscaping
  • Cleanout installation, if none exists
  • Permit and restoration needs

DIY vs. calling a pro

You can pour a bucket of water into a floor drain or toilet to see if it backs up elsewhere, and check whether only one drain is slow. A single slow drain is often a local clog. Several slow drains at once point to the lateral. Don't rent a power auger for a suspected broken pipe; it can make a crack worse. Call a pro when sewage backs up, smells persist, or clogs return after cleaning.

Florida licensing and permit notes

Florida law places sanitary sewer lines within the plumbing contractor's scope, including the digging that goes with it. Ask for the provider's license number and check it on the DBPR license search. Sewer replacements usually need a permit and an inspection.

Local note

Local note: older neighborhoods in Bradenton and Venice often have cast iron or clay sewer pipe. In Nokomis, some homes on older lots may be on septic, which changes who you call.

Sewer Line Repair questions

How do I know if my sewer line is broken?

Several slow drains at once, sewage smells, gurgling toilets and a very green or soggy patch of lawn are common signs. A camera inspection confirms the problem and its location.

What is a sewer camera inspection?

A waterproof camera on a flexible cable is pushed through the line from a cleanout. It shows cracks, roots, sags and breaks, and measures how far away each one is.

Is sewer lining as good as replacement?

Lining can last a long time when the old pipe still holds its shape. It is not a fit for collapsed pipes or bad sags, which usually need replacement.

Who is responsible for the sewer line to my house?

In most areas, the owner maintains the lateral on private property and the utility maintains the public main. Check your utility's rules for the exact dividing point.

Can tree roots really break a sewer line?

Roots usually enter through cracks or loose joints, then grow and widen them. Over time they can block the pipe or crack it further.

Does insurance cover a broken sewer line?

Standard policies often exclude the pipe itself. Some insurers offer a service line or sewer backup endorsement. Ask your agent.
